pubchem.title: PubChem Periodic Table of Elements and element pages
pubchem.citation: PubChem, National Center for Biotechnology Information, U.S. National Library of Medicine. Periodic Table of Elements. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/periodic-table/
pubchem.notes: REST: rest/pug/periodictable/JSON (one request) and rest/pug_view/data/element/{Z}/JSON (one per element). PubChem aggregates data from Jefferson Lab and Los Alamos National Laboratory (both U.S. DOE); the oxidation-state lists used here come from those two contributors via PubChem.

hsdb.title: Hazardous Substances Data Bank (HSDB), records of the elemental substances in PubChem
hsdb.licence: Public domain (U.S. Government work, National Library of Medicine)
hsdb.citation: Hazardous Substances Data Bank (HSDB), U.S. National Library of Medicine, via PubChem (National Center for Biotechnology Information): compound records of the elemental substances, sections Stability/Shelf Life, Other Experimental Properties and Reactivities and Incompatibilities. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/source/hsdb
hsdb.notes: tools/fetch_pubchem_hsdb.py caches the 'Experimental Properties' part of the PubChem record of each elemental substance (found by name). The reactivity notes in tools/curated/chemistry.toml restate what these records say in our own words; no HSDB sentence is copied. The build checks that each note citing hsdb has an HSDB record behind it.

cameo_chemicals.title: CAMEO Chemicals (NOAA), records of the elemental substances in PubChem
cameo_chemicals.licence: Free for use (U.S. NOAA); facts restated in our own words, no text copied — some CAMEO data is under its providers' copyright
cameo_chemicals.citation: CAMEO Chemicals, Office of Response and Restoration, U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, with the U.S. EPA, via PubChem: sections Air and Water Reactions and Reactive Group of the elemental substances. https://cameochemicals.noaa.gov/
cameo_chemicals.notes: tools/fetch_pubchem_hsdb.py caches the 'Stability and Reactivity' part of each elemental substance's PubChem record, where CAMEO Chemicals describes reactions with air and water. Used only as the grounding of our own-words notes in tools/curated/chemistry.toml.

pubchem_compounds.title: PubChem Compound records (formulas of named compounds)
pubchem_compounds.citation: PubChem, National Center for Biotechnology Information, U.S. National Library of Medicine: compound records found by name (PUG REST compound/name/{name}/property/MolecularFormula). https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/
pubchem_compounds.notes: Every compound in tools/curated/chemistry.toml that cites this source is looked up by its name (or by the row's `lookup` name); a compound whose PubChem molecular formula has different element counts from ours is left out and reported, and the record's CID is stored with each one that matches.

shannon1976.title: Shannon's effective ionic radii
shannon1976.citation: R. D. Shannon, Revised effective ionic radii and systematic studies of interatomic distances in halides and chalcogenides, Acta Crystallographica A32, 751–767 (1976), doi:10.1107/S0567739476001551.
shannon1976.notes: Effective ionic radii (not crystal radii) of the ions in the elements' common oxidation states, in tools/curated/ionic_radii.toml, transcribed via the mendeleev package 1.3.0 (MIT), whose metadata cites Shannon (1976) for this table (and Lundberg 2016 for some additions, not marked per row). Not re-checked against the printed table.

greenwood1997.title: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements
greenwood1997.citation: N. N. Greenwood and A. Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd edition, Butterworth-Heinemann, Oxford (1997), ISBN 978-0-7506-3365-9, doi:10.1016/C2009-0-30414-6.
greenwood1997.notes: Cited for mainstream, textbook-level facts in tools/curated/chemistry.toml (bonding type of the element, well-known compounds, reactivity where no HSDB or CAMEO record exists). Statements are our own words.

turler2013.title: Advances in the production and chemistry of the heaviest elements
turler2013.citation: A. Türler and V. Pershina, Advances in the production and chemistry of the heaviest elements, Chem. Rev. 113, 1237–1312 (2013), doi:10.1021/cr3002438.
turler2013.notes: Cited in tools/curated/chemistry.toml for what is (and is not) known of the chemistry of Z = 104-117: single-atom experiments and predictions. Statements are our own words.

pubchem_ghs.title: PubChem compound records — GHS Classification of the elemental substances
pubchem_ghs.licence: PubChem: public domain (U.S. Government work); the classifications are facts reported by their contributors (EU CLP Annex VI; ECHA C&L Inventory notifications, reuse with acknowledgement)
pubchem_ghs.citation: PubChem, National Center for Biotechnology Information, U.S. National Library of Medicine, compound records of the elemental substances, section 'GHS Classification' (rest/pug_view/data/compound/{CID}/JSON?heading=GHS+Classification); classifications from Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Annex VI, and from the notifications to the ECHA C&L Inventory as aggregated by PubChem.
pubchem_ghs.notes: One name lookup (rest/pug/compound/name/{name}/cids/JSON) and one GHS request per element, 2 per second. Shown: the EU harmonised classification where one exists, otherwise PubChem's aggregation of the ECHA C&L notifications with the most reports (with the share of reports behind each hazard statement, and the share that says the substance does not meet the GHS criteria), otherwise the first other contributor. GHS has no hazard class for radioactivity.

nist_gsie.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database — Ionization Energies
nist_gsie.licence: Public domain (U.S. Government work); citation requested
nist_gsie.citation: Kramida, A., Ralchenko, Yu., Reader, J. and NIST ASD Team (2024). NIST Atomic Spectra Database (version 5.12), [Online]. Available: https://physics.nist.gov/asd. National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD. DOI: https://doi.org/10.18434/T4W30F
nist_gsie.notes: All spectra H–Og requested in one CSV. The database covers neutral atoms up to Z = 108 (Hs); for Z ≥ 109 it lists nothing. Square brackets mark semi-empirical (interpolated/extrapolated) values, parentheses mark ab-initio theoretical values (ASD help text).

nist_levels.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database — Energy Levels
nist_levels.licence: Public domain (U.S. Government work); citation requested
nist_levels.citation: Kramida, A., Ralchenko, Yu., Reader, J. and NIST ASD Team (2024). NIST Atomic Spectra Database (version 5.12), [Online]. Available: https://physics.nist.gov/asd. DOI: https://doi.org/10.18434/T4W30F
nist_levels.notes: One tab-delimited request per neutral atom (108 answer). public/data/levels/{Z}.json keeps the lowest 60 levels with absolute energies and the ionization limit.

nist_lines.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database — Lines
nist_lines.licence: Public domain (U.S. Government work); citation requested
nist_lines.citation: Kramida, A., Ralchenko, Yu., Reader, J. and NIST ASD Team (2024). NIST Atomic Spectra Database (version 5.12), [Online]. Available: https://physics.nist.gov/asd. DOI: https://doi.org/10.18434/T4W30F
nist_lines.notes: 380-780 nm for the neutral atom and the singly charged ion (air wavelengths, as ASD gives them between 200 and 2000 nm), strongest 400 lines per species kept; plus vacuum windows around each laser-cooling line, whose A_ki gives the linewidth.

nist_awic.title: NIST Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions with Relative Atomic Masses
nist_awic.licence: Public domain (U.S. Government work); citation requested
nist_awic.citation: Coursey, J. S., Schwab, D. J., Tsai, J. J. and Dragoset, R. A., Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions (version 4.1). National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD. https://physics.nist.gov/Comp
nist_awic.notes: Linearized ASCII output, all elements, all isotopes. The standard atomic weights in this database are the IUPAC 2013 values (Meija et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 88, 265 (2016)); later IUPAC revisions are in `ciaaw`.

nist_srd141.title: NIST SRD 141 — Atomic Reference Data for Electronic Structure Calculations
nist_srd141.licence: Public domain (U.S. Government work); citation requested
nist_srd141.citation: Kotochigova, S., Levine, Z. H., Shirley, E. L., Stiles, M. D. and Clark, C. W., Atomic Reference Data for Electronic Structure Calculations, NIST Standard Reference Database 141. https://math.nist.gov/DFTdata/atomdata/
nist_srd141.notes: Per-element tables at math.nist.gov/DFTdata/atomdata/tables/, Z = 1-92. Orbital eigenvalues of the neutral atom in LDA and ScRLDA, converted from hartree to eV with CODATA. The Sm page prints its ScRLDA column one row out of step; that column is not used for Sm.

nist_codata.title: CODATA 2022 recommended values of the fundamental physical constants
nist_codata.licence: Public domain (U.S. Government work); citation requested
nist_codata.citation: E. Tiesinga, P. J. Mohr, D. B. Newell and B. N. Taylor (2024), "The 2022 CODATA Recommended Values of the Fundamental Physical Constants" (Web Version 9.0). National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD. https://physics.nist.gov/constants
nist_codata.notes: ASCII table https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/Table/allascii.txt. Generates src/physics/constants.ts and the eV ↔ kJ/mol factor used by the pipeline.

iaea_livechart.title: IAEA LiveChart of Nuclides — ground-state data
iaea_livechart.licence: Free for use; cite ENSDF and the IAEA Nuclear Data Section
iaea_livechart.citation: IAEA Nuclear Data Section, LiveChart of Nuclides, data API https://nds.iaea.org/relnsd/v1/data (ground states of all nuclides), based on ENSDF.
iaea_livechart.notes: One CSV request: ?fields=ground_states&nuclides=all. Used in M0 for natural abundances, nuclear spins and half-lives (most-stable mass number, radioactivity, hyperfine applicability).

ciaaw.title: IUPAC CIAAW — Standard Atomic Weights (2024) and abridged values
ciaaw.licence: Scientific facts; cite the IUPAC Commission on Isotopic Abundances and Atomic Weights
ciaaw.citation: IUPAC Commission on Isotopic Abundances and Atomic Weights, Standard Atomic Weights (2024) https://www.ciaaw.org/atomic-weights.htm and Abridged Standard Atomic Weights https://www.ciaaw.org/abridged-atomic-weights.htm
ciaaw.notes: Added in M0 (not in the SPEC §6.1 list). Supplies the single display value for elements whose standard atomic weight is an interval, and a cross-check of NIST AWIC against the current IUPAC table.

si_brochure.title: The International System of Units (SI Brochure), 9th edition
si_brochure.citation: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, The International System of Units (SI), 9th edition (2019), Section 2.2: the caesium-133 hyperfine transition frequency Δν_Cs = 9 192 631 770 Hz exactly.
si_brochure.notes: Added in M0. Source of exact defining values (Δν_Cs); also the definition of the degree Celsius used in src/physics/units.ts.

iupac_redbook_2005.title: Nomenclature of Inorganic Chemistry — IUPAC Recommendations 2005 (Red Book)
iupac_redbook_2005.citation: N. G. Connelly, T. Damhus, R. M. Hartshorn and A. T. Hutton (eds.), Nomenclature of Inorganic Chemistry — IUPAC Recommendations 2005, RSC Publishing, 2005, Table I (names of the elements).
iupac_redbook_2005.notes: Added in M0. IUPAC element spellings (aluminium, caesium) where PubChem uses U.S. spellings.

bipm_frequencies.title: BIPM — Recommended values of standard frequencies
bipm_frequencies.licence: © BIPM; numerical values are facts; cite
bipm_frequencies.citation: BIPM, Recommended values of standard frequencies for applications including the practical realization of the metre and secondary representations of the second (CCL-CCTF list, 2025 update), https://www.bipm.org/en/publications/mises-en-pratique/standard-frequencies — machine-readable via the BIPM Time Department CCL-CCTF API, https://webtai.bipm.org/api/ccl-cctf/
bipm_frequencies.notes: Every atomic and atomic-ion entry valid on the retrieval date, plus iodine (127I2) and the He-Ne laser. The rubidium-87 ground-state hyperfine splitting shown on its tile is this list's value.

bunge_rhf.title: Roothaan–Hartree–Fock ground-state atomic wavefunctions, He–Xe
bunge_rhf.citation: C. F. Bunge, J. A. Barrientos and A. V. Bunge, At. Data Nucl. Data Tables 53, 113 (1993).

mclean_rhf.title: Roothaan–Hartree–Fock atomic wavefunctions, Z = 55–92
mclean_rhf.citation: A. D. McLean and R. S. McLean, At. Data Nucl. Data Tables 26, 197 (1981).
mclean_rhf.notes: v0.2 (Tier B orbitals). DOI to be confirmed when the data is transcribed.

slater1930.title: Slater's rules for atomic screening constants
slater1930.citation: J. C. Slater, Atomic shielding constants, Phys. Rev. 36, 57–64 (1930), doi:10.1103/PhysRev.36.57.
slater1930.notes: Computed in the app (src/physics/zeff.ts) for subshells the Clementi–Raimondi table does not cover: hydrogen (where the rules give the exact Z = 1), elements beyond radon, and subshells outside the configuration Clementi and Raimondi used (e.g. gadolinium's 5d).

clementi_zeff.title: Clementi–Raimondi effective nuclear charges
clementi_zeff.citation: E. Clementi and D. L. Raimondi, J. Chem. Phys. 38, 2686 (1963), doi:10.1063/1.1733573; E. Clementi, D. L. Raimondi and W. P. Reinhardt, J. Chem. Phys. 47, 1300 (1967), doi:10.1063/1.1712084.
clementi_zeff.notes: tools/curated/zeff.toml (He-Rn): Z_eff = n x zeta, taken from the transcription of both tables in the MIT-licensed mendeleev package (v1.3.0, table screeningconstants); closed-shell atoms were recomputed independently as a check (agreement 1e-4 for He-Ar, 0.013 for Zn and Kr). Slater's rules are used for Z > 86.

schwerdtfeger2019.title: Table of static dipole polarizabilities of the neutral elements (Schwerdtfeger & Nagle)
schwerdtfeger2019.citation: P. Schwerdtfeger and J. K. Nagle, 2018 Table of static dipole polarizabilities of the neutral elements in the periodic table, Mol. Phys. 117, 1200-1225 (2019), doi:10.1080/00268976.2018.1535143.
schwerdtfeger2019.notes: tools/curated/polarizability.toml: the recommended value and its uncertainty for all 118 elements, in atomic units, transcribed via the MIT-licensed mendeleev package (v1.3.0), whose metadata cites the table as updated by its authors in 2023.

fock1935.title: Fock: the hidden four-dimensional symmetry of the hydrogen atom
fock1935.citation: V. Fock, Zur Theorie des Wasserstoffatoms, Z. Phys. 98, 145-154 (1935), doi:10.1007/BF01336904.
fock1935.notes: Cited by the symmetry note of the mathematical panel: hydrogen's 2n² degeneracy as an SO(4) symmetry.

barut1967.title: Barut & Kleinert: the hydrogen atom from a noncompact dynamical group
barut1967.citation: A. O. Barut and H. Kleinert, Transition probabilities of the hydrogen atom from noncompact dynamical groups, Phys. Rev. 156, 1541-1545 (1967), doi:10.1103/PhysRev.156.1541.
barut1967.notes: Cited by the symmetry note of the mathematical panel: all hydrogen levels in one representation of SO(4,2).

steck_alkali.title: Alkali D Line Data (Daniel A. Steck)
steck_alkali.licence: Compiled reference data; cite the sheet and revision
steck_alkali.citation: D. A. Steck, Alkali D Line Data (sodium, rubidium 85, rubidium 87, cesium), available online at https://steck.us/alkalidata/ — cite the sheet and its revision number.

allegrini2022.title: Survey of hyperfine measurements in alkali atoms
allegrini2022.citation: M. Allegrini, E. Arimondo and L. A. Orozco, Survey of hyperfine structure measurements in alkali atoms, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 51, 043102 (2022), arXiv:2209.11423.
allegrini2022.notes: Ground-state A constants of Li, Na, K, Rb-85 and Fr read from its Tables I-IV and VIII.

arimondo1977.title: Experimental determinations of the hyperfine structure in the alkali atoms
arimondo1977.citation: E. Arimondo, M. Inguscio and P. Violino, Rev. Mod. Phys. 49, 31 (1977).

vald_hfs.title: VALD hyperfine-structure constants (database description)
vald_hfs.licence: Scientific facts; cite the primary papers
vald_hfs.citation: arXiv:1911.03189 (database description); values are taken from the primary papers it cites.

olmschenk_catalog.title: Catalog of laser-cooled atoms and ions (S. Olmschenk)
olmschenk_catalog.licence: Cite; verify each entry against its primary reference
olmschenk_catalog.citation: S. Olmschenk, Laser-cooled atoms and ions catalog, https://personal.denison.edu/~olmschenks/atom_catalog.html and ion_catalog.html.
olmschenk_catalog.notes: Species list and first-trapping references for tools/curated/lasercooling.toml (read 2026-10-21); every milestone there carries its own DOI, checked against Crossref.

images_of_elements.title: Images of elements (Jürgen Kummer)
images_of_elements.licence: CC BY 3.0 (attribution by link to the element page)
images_of_elements.citation: Jürgen Kummer, images-of-elements.com — photographs of the chemical elements, CC BY 3.0; each photo is credited with a link to its element page.
images_of_elements.notes: Element pages and photographs fetched by tools/fetch_images.py; the choice per element is tools/curated/images.toml. The site's licence is CC BY 3.0 'unless otherwise noted': photos the page credits to someone else carry that credit and licence instead.

commons.title: Wikimedia Commons
commons.licence: Per-file licences; only the allow-list in SPEC §15.3
commons.citation: Wikimedia Commons; each file credited individually in CREDITS.md.
commons.notes: Only files pinned in tools/curated/images.toml, for elements images-of-elements.com cannot show freely. Commons rate-limits shared addresses heavily; the fetcher honours Retry-After.

usgs_mcs.title: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries
usgs_mcs.citation: U.S. Geological Survey, 2026, Mineral commodity summaries 2026 (ver. 1.3, May 2026), doi:10.3133/mcs2026; data: Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 Data Release, doi:10.5066/P1WKQ63T (file MCS2026_Commodities_Data.csv).
usgs_mcs.notes: World production and U.S. price or unit value per element for 2025 (USGS estimates), year-stamped, in tools/curated/production.toml; every number keeps its CSV line. Data release licence: CC0. Prices are per kg of the material named (often an oxide, ore or alloy), as USGS gives them.

jrc_foresight2023.title: Supply chain analysis and material demand forecast in strategic technologies and sectors in the EU – A foresight study
jrc_foresight2023.citation: S. Carrara et al., Supply chain analysis and material demand forecast in strategic technologies and sectors in the EU – A foresight study, JRC132889, Publications Office of the European Union, Luxembourg (2023), doi:10.2760/386650.
jrc_foresight2023.notes: Added after v0.1.0. tools/curated/sectors.toml: which raw materials the technologies of the renewable-energy, e-mobility, energy-intensive-industry and ICT sectors use (Tables 7–10), for the maps Essential for energy, for logistics & infrastructure and for IT, computing & telecom. Read from the open PDF (cached in tools/raw/sectors/).

eu_crm.title: EU critical and strategic raw materials (Critical Raw Materials Act, 2024)
eu_crm.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1252 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 (Critical Raw Materials Act), OJ L 2024/1252, 3.5.2024, CELEX 32024R1252: Annex I Section 1 (strategic) and Annex II Section 1 (critical raw materials); group memberships from the Commission's Study on the Critical Raw Materials for the EU 2023, doi:10.2873/725585.
eu_crm.notes: Raw materials mapped to elements in tools/curated/critical_raw_materials.toml; mappings through a mineral (coking coal and graphite, fluorspar, baryte) are marked, and osmium (platinum-group metal, not assessed) is flagged doubtful.

cie_cmf.title: CIE 1931 colour-matching functions, 2° standard colorimetric observer
cie_cmf.licence: Cited standard table (CIE 018:2019, Table 6; ISO/CIE 11664-1:2019); the CIE's data file is CC BY-SA 4.0
cie_cmf.citation: CIE (2019), Colour-matching functions of CIE 1931 standard colorimetric observer (data table), International Commission on Illumination, Vienna, doi:10.25039/CIE.DS.xvudnb9b; values from CIE 018:2019, The Basis of Physical Photometry, 3rd ed., Table 6, doi:10.25039/TR.018.2019.
cie_cmf.notes: The standard observer x̄, ȳ, z̄ on the 5 nm grid 380–780 nm (SPEC §11.6), used as the numerical values of the international standard, with citation. The file's SHA-256 is checked against the CIE's own metadata record. Written to public/data/cie1931.json for the spectrum colours.

cod.title: Crystallography Open Database
cod.citation: S. Gražulis et al., Crystallography Open Database – an open-access collection of crystal structures, J. Appl. Cryst. 42, 726–729 (2009), doi:10.1107/S0021889809016690; each structure is cited by its COD id and original reference.
cod.notes: One CIF per element, read into tools/curated/crystal.toml (space group, Pearson symbol, cell lengths and angles, temperature where stated). Entries from before 1947 are avoided because of the old kX unit.

crc_handbook.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 95th edition — Heat capacity of the elements at 25 °C
crc_handbook.licence: Cited scientific table (numerical values are facts; cite)
crc_handbook.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 95th edition, CRC Press, Boca Raton (2014), doi:10.1201/b17118, section 4, 'Heat capacity of the elements at 25 °C'; values as transcribed in the mendeleev package 1.3.0 (MIT), whose property metadata cites this edition.
crc_handbook.notes: Molar heat capacity C_p at 25 °C and 1 bar in tools/curated/thermal.toml, per mole of atoms, or of molecules for H2, N2, O2, F2, Cl2, Br2 and I2 as the table gives them. Transcribed once from mendeleev; not checked line by line against the printed handbook.

lodders2025.title: Solar System elemental abundances from the solar photosphere and CI-chondrites
lodders2025.citation: K. Lodders, M. Bergemann and H. Palme, Solar System elemental abundances from the solar photosphere and CI-chondrites, Space Sci. Rev. 221, 23 (2025), doi:10.1007/s11214-025-01146-w.
lodders2025.notes: Table 6 (atoms per 10^6 Si and log ε, present and proto-solar, with 1σ) and Table A13 of the Electronic Supplementary Material (proto-solar mass fractions), copied as printed into the [[solar]] table of tools/curated/abundance.toml. Successor to Lodders (2021), which is not open access. The Sm row of Table A13 is corrupted in the source and is left out; the Co mass fraction disagrees slightly with its own atom count and is flagged.

kobayashi2020.title: The origin of elements from carbon to uranium
kobayashi2020.citation: C. Kobayashi, A. I. Karakas and M. Lugaro, The origin of elements from carbon to uranium, ApJ 900, 179 (2020), doi:10.3847/1538-4357/abae65, arXiv:2008.04660.
kobayashi2020.notes: tools/curated/nucleosynthesis.toml; every value flagged estimated (approximate transcription).

pyykko2011.title: A suggested periodic table up to Z ≤ 172
pyykko2011.citation: P. Pyykkö, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 13, 161 (2011).

karshenboim2005.title: Precision physics of simple atoms: QED tests, nuclear structure and fundamental constants
karshenboim2005.citation: S. G. Karshenboim, Phys. Rep. 422, 1 (2005), doi:10.1016/j.physrep.2005.08.008, arXiv:hep-ph/0509010.
karshenboim2005.notes: Added in M2. Ground-state (1s) hyperfine intervals of hydrogen, deuterium and tritium, read from its table of measured values (each row names the primary measurement).

primary_literature.title: Primary research papers (one per row, by DOI)
primary_literature.citation: The paper named by the DOI (or arXiv identifier) given with each value; listed in full in PROVENANCE.md.
primary_literature.notes: Added in M2. Used where a value comes from a single research paper rather than from a compilation; the value's own record carries the DOI. Every DOI was checked against Crossref.

cgpm_resolutions.title: Resolutions of the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM)
cgpm_resolutions.citation: Conférence Générale des Poids et Mesures, Resolutions (BIPM), each cited by its DOI 10.59161/CGPM<year>RES<n>E.
cgpm_resolutions.notes: Added in M2. The definitions, prototypes and dates in tools/curated/si_history.toml and the timeline of the second in tools/curated/clocks.toml; texts read on bipm.org.

bipm_mep_kilogram.title: Mise en pratique for the definition of the kilogram in the SI (SI Brochure, Appendix 2)
bipm_mep_kilogram.citation: CCM, Mise en pratique for the definition of the kilogram in the SI, SI Brochure 9th edition, Appendix 2 (BIPM).
bipm_mep_kilogram.notes: Added in M2. The X-ray-crystal-density realization of the kilogram with silicon-28 spheres.

allen_en.title: Configuration energies (Allen electronegativity) of the elements
allen_en.citation: J. B. Mann, T. L. Meek and L. C. Allen, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 122, 2780 (2000), doi:10.1021/ja992866e; J. B. Mann, T. L. Meek, E. T. Knight, J. F. Capitani and L. C. Allen, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 122, 5132 (2000), doi:10.1021/ja9928677.
allen_en.notes: Added in M2. tools/curated/electronegativity_allen.toml: configuration energies in eV, as transcribed in the MIT-licensed mendeleev package (v1.3.0). For He and groups 1-2 they equal the first ionization energy (checked against NIST to 0.003 eV, except H and Cs). Not converted to the Pauling-like scale.

marschner2023.title: Marschner's Mineral Nutrition of Plants, 4th edition
marschner2023.citation: Z. Rengel, I. Cakmak and P. J. White (eds.), Marschner's Mineral Nutrition of Plants, 4th ed., Academic Press (2023), doi:10.1016/C2019-0-00491-8; chapters cited by DOI.
marschner2023.notes: Which elements are essential or beneficial for plants and what they do (tools/curated/biology.toml, moved from the 3rd edition of 2012 after v0.1.0), and the plant details in tools/curated/plants.toml: uptake form, mobility in the phloem (Table 3.8), the concentration in shoots sufficient for growth (Table 1.3), the year each micronutrient was shown to be essential (Table 1.1), signs of too little and too much, soils, crop quality. Facts only, in our own words; checked against the text of the 4th edition (Fin's copy). Chapter DOIs checked against Crossref.

mengel_kirkby2001.title: Principles of Plant Nutrition, 5th edition
mengel_kirkby2001.citation: K. Mengel and E. A. Kirkby (with H. Kosegarten and T. Appel), Principles of Plant Nutrition, 5th ed., Kluwer Academic Publishers, Dordrecht (2001), doi:10.1007/978-94-010-1009-2; chapters cited by DOI.
mengel_kirkby2001.notes: Added after v0.1.0. tools/curated/plants.toml: the four groups of plant nutrients by their biochemical job (chapter 1), the leaf levels of maize and apple classed from deficient to excess (Tables 2.20 and 2.21), soils and fertilisers. Facts only, in our own words; checked against the text of the 5th edition (Fin's copy). Chapter DOIs checked against Crossref.

barker_pilbeam2015.title: Handbook of Plant Nutrition, 2nd edition
barker_pilbeam2015.citation: A. V. Barker and D. J. Pilbeam (eds.), Handbook of Plant Nutrition, 2nd ed., CRC Press, Boca Raton (2015), doi:10.1201/b18458; one chapter per element, cited by its chapter DOI.
barker_pilbeam2015.notes: Added after v0.1.0. tools/curated/plants.toml: leaf levels of crops and trees from the element chapters' tables (for zinc and iron the usual ranges by group of plants, which the book takes from Bryson et al. 2014), and notes on beneficial elements. binkley_fisher2020.title: Ecology and Management of Forest Soils, 5th edition

binkley_fisher2020.notes: Added after v0.1.0. tools/curated/plants.toml: nutrients in forests (Table 8.3) and the foliar levels below which trees often respond to fertiliser (Table 13.2). epstein1972.title: Mineral Nutrition of Plants: Principles and Perspectives
epstein1972.citation: E. Epstein, Mineral Nutrition of Plants: Principles and Perspectives, John Wiley & Sons, New York (1972), ISBN 0-471-24340-X.
epstein1972.notes: Added after v0.1.0. tools/curated/plants.toml: history (the tests for an essential element; the elements known to be essential by the end of the 19th century) and the ecology of wild plants (indicator and accumulator plants, serpentine and salty soils). Never used for an element's present status: the book predates, for example, the discovery that nickel is essential. Facts only, in our own words.
